quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When driving down a long or steep hill, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors for fast-moving traffic behind you.
Assume all traffic is moving at the same speed.
Look over your shoulder for traffic behind you.
Press down on your brake pedal to control other drivers' speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for fast-moving traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors for vehicles moving fast when driving down hills. Vehicles go faster on steep slopes. Watch for large trucks and buses that may be speeding.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. You should:

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers let you through.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If a car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If your wheels drop onto the road shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car at the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without braking. Then carefully turn back onto the road. Watch for other traffic as you re-enter the road.

questions.question: What driving technique helps you avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highway as fast as possible.
Turn on four-wheel drive.
Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snowy or icy roads. This and increasing your distance from other cars are the best ways to avoid crashes in winter weather.

questions.question: Turning your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Not necessary.
Not needed if you use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: If you see this sign, you:

options.text: Cannot pass another vehicle.
May pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
May pass if you know the road ahead.
May pass only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white and rectangular with black markings. You must obey all regulatory signs. This sign means passing other vehicles is not allowed.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Stops distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to sudden problems.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to sudden problems.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between your vehicle and others. This gives you enough time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: You are in an accident and someone is injured. You should:

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them the wrong way can make minor injuries serious. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, use direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Turn on your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who might not see you. For example, sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
Speed up as fast as you can.
Back up slowly.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, let pedestrians and other traffic still in the intersection finish crossing or moving.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, a small vehicle driver must be prepared for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Extra air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Small vehicle drivers should be ready to steer carefully when passing large vehicles, especially at high speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the direction traffic must move on this street. You must drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas
When driving in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly blocks the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you stop the normal flow of traffic. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
Directly behind your vehicle.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are usually on the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and get ready to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before going.
May drive through if the intersection is clear.
May not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through if the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if it is clear. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must let pedestrians cross first at any intersection, whether or not there is a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are open for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as fast as you can.
Slow down, move over to clear a path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move over to clear a path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle siren or lights, slow down, move your vehicle to clear a path, and stop. Do not try to race the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: Which is a trait of a defensive driver?

options.text: Anticipation
Passivity
Easy to distract
Anger

questions.correctAnswerText: Anticipation
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers stay a safe distance behind other vehicles. They predict what might happen on the road and take action to avoid problems.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is dropping off children:

options.text: Do not go until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm out, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: What happens if you refuse to take an alcohol test?

options.text: Your license will be suspended.
It is your right and nothing will happen.
It is recommended.
You will go to jail for one night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: When you drive a motor vehicle, you agree to take an alcohol test if an officer asks. If you refuse, your license will be suspended for 365 days on your first offense. For a second or later offense, it will be suspended for 730 days.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: Your tires become less effective as you drive faster.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slowing down makes the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires become less effective as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster on a wet road, your tires cannot remove water from the surface. If you go too fast, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane—sliding on a layer of water.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only blood alcohol above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only blood alcohol above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills suffer with any amount of alcohol. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Emergency vehicles ahead.
Uncontrolled intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up.

questions.question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Use tires with proper air pressure.
Replace worn tires.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your car slides on a layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase the risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: When an oncoming car is on the left and a bicyclist is on the right, you should:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. When there is a bicyclist on the right you want to pass and an oncoming car on the left, do not try to squeeze between both. Instead, let the car pass first, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: It is best to keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep empty space around all sides of your vehicle. This gives you time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: It is summer.
You must immediately stop and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to get through the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn that work is being done on or next to the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: Louisiana law requires headlights to be used:

options.text: When the driver is tired.
Between sunset and sunrise.
When the temperature drops below freezing.
During daytime in good weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between sunset and sunrise.
questions.explanation: Louisiana law requires headlights between sunset and sunrise. Use low beams when within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or 200 feet behind another vehicle.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means stop before entering the intersection, at any stop line, and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: Characteristics of drivers with road rage include:

options.text: Deliberately blocking other vehicles.
Flashing headlights.
Cutting off or swerving in front of other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Road rage behaviors include blocking other drivers, tailgating, flashing headlights, cutting off or swerving in front of drivers, following another vehicle, and threatening or rude communication. If you see these actions, give the driver space and do not respond.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your car and walk for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is also unsafe.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it mean on a sign?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
An action is forbidden.
Some drivers should yield to other drivers.
Drive under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means an action is forbidden. These signs are rectangular and white with red and black markings. A red circle and slash on top of a symbol means that action is not allowed.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side that traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road where they can see traffic coming toward them.

questions.question: What is an inattentive driver?

options.text: A driver who looks at things off the road or daydreams.
A driver who looks at a passenger instead of the road.
A driver who only watches the car ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not look at passengers, search for things in your car, read, sightsee, or daydream while driving. Keep scanning the road, checking your mirrors, and looking at your gauges. These safe habits will help you stay focused as a driver.

questions.question: When turning, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: When turning, slow down to a speed where you can control your car, stay in your lane, and react to anything unexpected.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Both directions can pass if it is safe. Only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Drive normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, give them the right-of-way, and then proceed carefully. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: When driving in rain, what lights must you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down because the road changes direction sharply.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road changes direction sharply.
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead will turn sharply (in this case, to the right). Slow down before the sharp curve as you would at an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign tells you to slow down at the intersection ahead and be ready to stop. Yield to other drivers and pedestrians. You may go when it is safe.
